title: Stability Swarm — Weekly Playbook & Ownership Handover Template
summary: Working doc: concrete weekly "swarm" routine to accelerate SLO remediation, hand over partial ownership, and capture short experiments. Includes templates for the on-call to pair with product/infra owners and a lightweight handoff checklist for stepped escalation.
body:
Context:
This doc captures a repeatable, 60–90 minute weekly "swarm" that brings together SREs, feature owners, infra, and product ops to make visible SLO drift, run short remediation experiments, and rotate temporary ownership. Goal is to reduce time-to-fix and prevent long-lived operational debt by creating a low-friction cross-functional ritual.

When to run:
- Cadence: weekly, 60–90 minutes
- Core window: Tue 10:00–11:30 PT (avoids Monday noise; aligns with APAC overlap)

(continued)
Participants (core):
- 2 SREs (facilitator + triage lead)
- 1 infra/serving-runtime engineer
- 1 product owner (hosted/dedicated/private depending on affected surface)
- 1 data/observability engineer (rotate)
- Optional: solutions eng / CS rep when customer impact in ticket backlog

Roles during swarm:
- Facilitator (SRE): runs the agenda, enforces timeboxes, finalizes ownership assignments.
- Triage lead (SRE): leads investigation, pulls traces and error graphs, proposes immediate mitigation.
- Owner rep (product/infra): reviews proposed mitigations for feasibility and decides on follow-up.
- Recorder: captures actions, owners, and experiments in the ticketing system.

Pre-read (30m before):
- Slack thread with top 3 SLO alerts + short histogram of token latency/error spikes.
- Link to dashboards: per-model latency SLO, tail-latency heatmap, error budget burn rate.

Sample agenda (90m):
- 0–10m: Quick state (alerts summary, recent deploys, capacity events).
- 10–35m: Deep-dive #1 (highest customer or SLO risk).
  - What: symptom, timeline, rollback risk, known PRs.
  - Quick data pulls: 95/99/99.9 latency, top callers, queue depth.
- 35–55m: Short experiment planning (prefers mitigations that can be validated within 24–72h).
  - Examples: routing to fallback model variant, reducing max_tokens, temporary autoscale policy change, KV cache invalidation check.
- 55–75m: Ownership assignments + handover template completion.
- 75–90m: Retro micro (what worked, blockers) + schedule follow-ups.

Ownership handover template (fill during swarm):
- Issue key / title: (Jira/Linear)
- Symptom summary (1–2 lines):
- SLOs impacted and current burn rate:
- Immediate mitigation (action owner, ETA):
- Short experiment (what to measure, success criteria, instrumentation owner):
- Rollback / exit criteria:
- Long-term owner assigned (team + contact):
- Next check-in (date/time):

Quick triage checklist (first 20 minutes):
- Is this a deploy-related regression? (check recent deploys, PR tags)
- Are there correlated infra events (GPU saturation, networking, DB throttling)?
- Has the cold-start/KV cache hit ratio changed?
- Can we route to a lower-capacity/compat model to reduce tail-latency?
- Are logs/trace samples available for representative requests?

Experiment catalog (examples we often reuse):
- Canary rollback to prior model build (measure 15–60m)
- Route 10–20% traffic to cached prefix path; monitor 95/99 latency for 2h
- Temp decrease min batch size to lower latency during peak (validate throughput impact)
- Adjust autoscaler threshold + surge config for 1–3h window

Communication templates (short snippets to post in incident channel or customer comms):
- Internal (short): "Swarm started for SLO drift on /v1/generate. Triage lead @sam. Quick mitigations: route fallbacks + spin extra workers. Updates in this thread every 30m."
- External (customer-facing): "We're investigating a recent increase in latency affecting some requests. We've applied temporary routing changes and expect stabilizing within X hours. We'll follow up with a timeline and full postmortem if needed."

Handoff rubric (how to pick long-term owner):
- If fix requires infra changes (kernel, scheduler, autoscaler): infra team owns.
- If fix requires prompt/model changes: serving-runtime or model-onboarding team owns.
- If fix is product-level (behavior change): product/feature team owns with SRE as reviewer.

Meeting artifacts and minimal ticket template fields (to reduce back-and-forth):
- Title, severity级, SLO impacted, current burn rate, immediate actions, experiment details, owner, ETA, monitoring dashboards, links to traces/logs, communications posted (timestamps).

Follow-up rhythm (after swarm):
- Day 0: validate mitigation — recorder posts initial result 6–12h after action.
- Day 1–3: short experiments run and measure; if stable, escalate to long-term backlog.
- Day 7: if unresolved, convene a deep-dive working group (2–3 sessions) with explicit engineering tasking.

Operational heuristics and guardrails:
- Prefer mitigations that are reversible and have observable KPIs within 2–72h.
- Avoid large config changes during customer business hours unless necessary.
- For repeated SLO drifts (>2 in 30 days) escalate to a reliability epic with SLA tracking.

Templates to copy into Jira/Linear (one-liners):
- "Swarm: [short symptom] — mitigation: [action] — owner: [team/name] — ETA: [hh:mm Z] — check-in: [date/time]"

Measurement guidance (what to report next swarm):
- 95th, 99th, 99.9th latency pre/post mitigation (absolute numbers + % change)
- Error budget consumed during window and projected weekly burn rate
- Cost delta (if mitigation uses additional capacity)

Open discussion items / TODOs in this doc:
- Automate pre-read dashboard snapshot (cron job to post graphs 30m before swarm). Owner: Observability team (María).
- Standardize experiment tagging in telemetry so we can filter swarm-run experiments. Owner: Data infra (Ibrahim).
- Create a rotation roster in HR-ops for cross-team coverage (quarterly). Owner: SRE lead (Claire).

Notes to self / facilitator tips:
- Keep interventions small; the goal is to reduce blast radius and learn fast.
- Push for explicit success/fail criteria for every quick experiment.
- Encourage product owners to bring a small list of 'do not touch' constraints (customer-facing contract boundaries).

Appendix: sample completed handover (realistic example)
- Issue: SRE-4927 "High tail latency on embeddings endpoint (2026-02-11)"
- Symptom: 99.9 latency increased 4x after model rollout 2026-02-10 22:14 UTC
- Impacted SLOs: embeddings.latency.99 <= 350ms (currently 1.4s), error budget burn 8%/hour
- Immediate mitigation: route 30% traffic to previous model variant (owner: Samuel, ETA 15m)
- Short experiment: enable prefix KV caching for hot prefixes + monitor 99th (owner: infra, ETA 2h)
- Rollback criteria: if 99.9 remains >800ms after 2h, rollback fully to previous model
- Long-term owner: serving-runtime (Claire)
- Next check-in: 2026-02-11 03:00 UTC

End of doc — use this as a replicable weekly ritual. Add your notes and copy the handover template into any ticket created during the swarm.
